items.title: Godot to ban (almost all) AI coding contributions
items.excerpt: The Godot Foundation updated its contribution policy to ban AI-generated code for substantial pieces of work, while still permitting narrow AI assists like code completion and regex helpers. A concrete engine-governance stance on how (and whether) generative AI belongs in a game-dev codebase: 'AI cannot take responsibility, and we can't trust heavy users of AI to understand their code enough to fix it.'

items.title: Slay the Spire 2 lead says the 'garbage' placeholder art is important and gen AI would ruin it
items.excerpt: Mega Crit's lead argues that deliberately rough hand-made placeholder art is a vital part of the early-access design process, and that swapping it for polished generative-AI art would distort how players judge an unfinished game. A working designer's craft case for why gen AI doesn't fit their iteration workflow.

items.title: Yoshitaka Amano Is More Centrist on AI Than You'd Hope
items.excerpt: Legendary Final Fantasy artist Yoshitaka Amano gives a notably measured take on generative AI in creative work, resisting a flat rejection. A prominent game-art voice weighing how AI intersects with hand-crafted illustration — useful context for how veteran creatives are positioning themselves on the tech.

items.title: 'Good games will get cloned and buried' – AI vibe coding is one of the biggest threats on storefronts like Steam, analyst warns
items.excerpt: An industry analyst warns that AI 'vibe coding' will let opportunists rapidly clone successful games and flood storefronts, burying originals under low-effort copies. A discoverability-and-design-economics angle on how fast generative tooling is changing what shipping a game on Steam looks like.

items.title: George Lucas Goes To The Dark Side, Says AI Is 'The Future'
items.excerpt: Star Wars creator George Lucas compares refusing to use AI to riding a horse in the age of cars, calling the tech inevitable for creative work. A high-profile creator framing generative AI as an unavoidable shift — the kind of stance shaping how studios and creatives debate adopting it.
